answer: In a market for tundra sensor data, every agent identity must lock a $100 bond for 30 days before bidding. Creating 1,000 fake identities therefore ties up $100,000; renaming agents cannot reuse funds already locked. The bond stays locked even when demand reaches its nadir. Through this economic prism, identities remain cheap to invent but costly to activate: an attacker must finance each account for the full lock period.
